scope: Proposition 4.1 (Local bound) of the manuscript “The Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions” (preprints/The-Kakeya-maximal-conjecture-in-three-dimensions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 074 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 49cc52aa3de89f0e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 24-25. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: After an extensive regular restriction, the mass of active original indices contained in any plank of widths 1 ≤ a ≤ b ≤ K over a dyadic temporal block of K = Nκ bins satisfies nI,W ≤exp T(κ, a, b), T(κ, a, b) = mN−Π(κ) K−H ad−1−H b1+H . (4.2) The bounds hold simultaneously at every fixed limiting scale and shape, under the finite-test and slow-diagonal convention of Section 2, and are inherited by further restrictions. Suppose conversely that, on an extensive graph, disjoint indexed-block assignments to planks of common widths a, b have masses at least T(κ, a, b) in exponent. Set a = logN a, u = logN (K/b), χ = a + u. (4.3) If χ < 1, the isotropic scale cut described below gives an ensemble at resolution N′ = Nb/(Ka) = N1−χ with matching sharp upper and lower bounds. At H = h0 = h this is an ensemble of exact 24 critical equalities, from which a realizing representative sequence can be selected. Its temporal profile is G(v) =      0, 0 ≤ v ≤ (κ − χ)/(1 − χ), F(χ + (1 − χ)v) − F(κ) 1 − χ , (κ − χ)/(1 − χ) ≤ v ≤ 1. (4.4)
